thread_text:
laura-support: Hi team — customer (ACME-devs) reporting 429s while their project quota tile shows available capacity. Repro steps below, attaching logs.

laura-support: Repro (from customer):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-ACME" -H "X-Project-ID: proj-acme-42" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  "error":"rate_limit_exceeded",
  "quota_scope":"org",
  "retry_after":12,
  "quota_used":125030,
  "quota_limit":125000
}
```

laura-support: Customer timeline: project-level tokens for proj-acme-42 show ~4k available in dashboard at 15:02 UTC, but they started seeing 429s at 15:04 UTC. Org-level ledger (they don't have direct org view) — our infra logs show org pool hit limit at 15:03:58 UTC.

laura-support: Screenshot links: https://img.redwood.test/XXX (project tile 15:02) and https://img.redwood.test/YYY (429 response from client)

emma-support: thanks — pinging @jake-engineering @maya-sre @anna-billing to triage. Is this the rolling-window off-by-timezone bug we've seen before or something new? :thinking_face:

jake-engineering: looking. Quick note: project tiles are computed from per-project rolling windows; org tiles are an aggregate of project ledgers but there is a separate org shared pool. Possible causes: (1) org shared pool consumption not reflected in project tile (we intentionally show per-project remaining to avoid noisy org details), (2) delay in ingestion pipeline for analytics -> dashboard stale by up to ~2m, (3) double-counting in org aggregation when projects use shared fanout.

maya-sre: I pulled the infra quota logs for org org-acme at 15:02-15:05 UTC:
```
2026-03-15T15:03:58Z quota-service org org-acme pool used=125000 limit=125000 source=dedicated-rates
2026-03-15T15:03:58Z quota-service project proj-acme-42 used=121000 limit=125000 source=project-commit
2026-03-15T15:03:59Z policy-eval decision=deny project=proj-acme-42 reason=org-shared-pool-empty
```

maya-sre: So org pool tripped first and denied at 15:03:59Z. The project's dashboard showed remaining because dashboard aggregation reads per-project ledger that lags ingestion by ~90-150s during peak and it doesn't show org-shared-pool state.

anna-billing: For invoices, metering is authoritative from the billing ledger (postback from quota-service). We should confirm whether any tokens were debited from org shared pool vs project commit — that affects which account was billed. I'll run the billing ledger query for that time range and share results.

laura-support: Customer is confused because their project UI tile said available. They escalated to legal/compliance — high urgency for a clear explanation and potential refund if misbilled.

chris-platform: Actionable items:
- eng (jake) to add an explicit org-shared-pool indicator on project tiles (UX) + show last-updated timestamp (P2)
- eng-infra (maya) to investigate ingestion delay and whether we can reduce dashboard staleness to <30s (P1)
- billing (anna) to verify ledger entries and flag any invoices/refunds (P1)
- support (laura/emma) to collect request ids and customer correlation ids for the period 15:00-15:10 UTC

jake-engineering: quick mitigation: add ephemeral banner for affected orgs that have org-shared-pool usage >90% until UX change shipped. I'll open a deploy PR for runtime gating to surface org pool status in admin API.

maya-sre: Root cause hypothesis: org-shared-pool consumption hit limit at 15:03:58Z; dashboard per-project tile read from the per-project ingestion stream that had ~1.5m lag due to a blocked Kafka partition during rebalancing. That explains discrepancy and the 429s.

laura-support: Collected request ids from customer: [req_0a1b2c, req_0a1b2d, req_0a1b2e] timestamps 2026-03-15T15:04:01Z → 15:04:12Z. Sending to maya/anna now.

anna-billing: Billing ledger extract (prelim): org-acme debit 125030 tokens at 2026-03-15T15:03:58Z, projects billed per their committed allocations. If customer was billed for org-shared usage but expects project-only, we need to reconcile contracts. I'll open a billing ticket and flag for reconciliation and potential proration.

jake-engineering: Filed GH issue: redwood/platform#9876 — "org-shared-pool visibility + dashboard stale indicator". Assigning to @chris-platform. Proposed timeline: hotfix (banner) within 24h, UX change in next sprint.

emma-support: Next steps for support: explain to customer that 429s were because the org-level shared pool hit its global limit; project tile only shows project ledger and can be stale up to ~2m under current ingestion load. Offer to credit tokens for time window while we investigate. cc @laura-support for customer msg draft.

laura-support: Draft to customer:
"Hi — thanks for flagging. We investigated and found your org's shared quota pool reached its limit at 15:03:58 UTC which caused API requests to be throttled, even though the project-level tile showed remaining tokens (that tile can lag briefly). We're offering a credit for the affected window while we improve dashboard visibility and ingestion latency. We're also implementing an on-page org pool indicator and reducing dashboard lag."

tom-customer: Thanks — appreciated. We'll gather any additional logs if needed. Please keep us posted and we want the credit noted in the invoice.

maya-sre: Follow-up: moving to P1 on ingestion pipeline. I see the Kafka partition rebalanced around 15:01:30Z and one consumer had a transient GC spike causing ~100-180s backlog. Remediation: bump consumer pool and add circuit detection alert on partition lag >60s. I'll create ops runbook.

jake-engineering: Also adding correlation-id passthrough header so support can map API responses to billing debits: X-Req-ID -> billing-entry.correlation_id. I'll land schema change, deploy small runtime bump.

laura-support: great. Closing thread for now; will reopen if customer requests escalation after billing ticket. Thanks all :raised_hands:

-- end thread --
